payload.name: Extract Encouragement and Supportive Utterances
payload.description: When a speaker offers encouragement, sympathy, advice, or reassurance to another person, extract it as an event or relationship memory, including the key content and any linked setback.
content: During extraction, treat supportive, encouraging, or advising messages as memory-worthy events: record the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of the support/advice (e.g., 'X told Y that rejections don't define her, keep trying').
If the support references a prior setback or difficulty (explicit or implied), link this event to that existing state/event memory.
Also evaluate whether the utterance reveals a relationship quality (e.g., supportive, caring) and update or create a relationship memory between the participants when appropriate.

solves: The Construction Agent sometimes fails to extract memories from messages that contain emotional support, encouragement, or advice, leaving such facts unpersisted and unanswerable later. This occurs because supportive utterances are not explicitly recognized as memory-worthy events or relationship cues. This skill applies whenever one participant offers reassurance, motivation, or guidance to another, especially after a setback or challenge, and guides extraction of the gist, the relationship signal, and any linked prior state.
